label: Etsy
terms_note: Automation allowed under the API Terms of Use; three app tiers since 2026-07 — Seller App (own shop, automated near-instant approval, no commercial use), Personal App (reviewed), Commercial Access (manual review, needed to serve OTHER sellers via OAuth); per-app QPS/QPD limits shown in the portal (x-limit-per-second / x-limit-per-day headers, 429 + retry-after); items must be seller-designed, AI use disclosed

reference.verdict: **Verdict** — has_api: **yes** (full listing API, verdict A stands).
auth: 1. Tenant registers an app at https://www.etsy.com/developers (Developer Portal). Tiers since 2026-07: **Seller App** — own
3. Access token lifetime **3600 s**; refresh token **90 days** (`grant_type=refresh_token`) — the connector's `_etsy_refresh` already does this.
4. Scopes: `listings_r listings_w listings_d shops_r shops_w transactions_r transactions_w profile_r profile_w email_r address_r address_w`.

endpoints.notes: required `quantity`, `title`, `description`, `price`, `who_made` (i_did / someone_else / collective), `when_made` (made_to_order / 2020_2026 …), `taxonomy_id`; `type` = physical / **download** / both; optional `tags[]` (13), `materials[]`, `image_ids[]`, `shop_section_id`, `should_auto_renew`, `is_t
multipart `file` (binary) or `listing_file_id`, `name`, `rank`; digital-file limit 20 MB (help centre; the connector already enforces `_ETSY_FILE_MAX`)
multipart `image` (binary, required) or `listing_image_id`, `rank` (default 1), `overwrite`, `is_watermarked`, `alt_text` — a build screenshot / cover satisfies "at least one image before activation"

`title`, `description`, `tags[]`, `taxonomy_id`, `image_ids[]`, `should_auto_renew`, `type`, `state` ∈ {`active`, `inactive`} — "Setting a `draft` listing to `active` will also publish the listing on etsy.com" (a $0.20 listing fee applies)

reference.limits: Per app key: QPS + rolling-24 h QPD, values shown in the Developer Portal (examples in the docs: 150 / s, 100 000 / day); headers `x-limit-per-second`, `x-remaining-this-second`, `x-limit-per-day`, `x-remaining-today`; 429 carries `retry-after`. - API Terms of Use (caching policy §1, no scraping, one app per purpose); Commercial Access reviewed by Etsy for any app that serves multiple sellers. Seller Apps: own shop only, automated approval. - Marketplace policy: items must be designed / made by the seller (`who_made = i_did`), AI involvement disclosed in the listing; digital downloads allowed
mcp_sdk: Community live-API MCPs: https://github.com/DColl/etsy-mcp-server, https://github.com/aserper/etsy-mcp (37 tools),
No official SDK; the OpenAPI 3 spec is the contract.

fields.name: client_id
fields.help: Etsy App API Key keystring (etsy.com/developers/your-apps); sent as client_id in the refresh grant form body (Etsy's refresh grant takes no client secret).

fields.name: api_key
fields.help: Value of the x-api-key header required on every v3 request: the keystring and the shared secret joined by a colon, e.g. 1aa2bb33c44d55eeeeee6fff:a1b2c3d4e5 (both on the Your Apps page).

fields.name: refresh_token
fields.help: Refresh token (numeric user id prefix, e.g. 12345678.JNGI...) from a one-time OAuth 2.0 authorization-code + PKCE consent at etsy.com/oauth/connect with scopes shops_r listings_r listings_w transactions_r; valid 90 days, after which the seller consents again. Access tokens (1 h) are minted from it. A refresh grant also returns a new refresh token, which replaces the old one. The runtime keeps a rotated refresh token in memory; set PLATFORM_MCP_STATE_DIR to also save it (<dir>/<platform>.json, mode 0600) so it is preferred over this variable on the next start. The state file is keyed by platform id, so it is shared with ecommerce_channels/etsy: give each server its own PLATFORM_MCP_STATE_DIR (or its own consent) so they never race on one rotating refresh token.

config_fields.name: shop_id
config_fields.help: Numeric Etsy shop id (GET /v3/application/users/me returns it as shop_id).

config_fields.name: taxonomy_id
config_fields.help: Seller taxonomy id every created listing is filed under (GET /v3/application/seller-taxonomy/nodes); required by create_product.

config_fields.name: who_made
config_fields.help: createDraftListing who_made for new listings: i_did | someone_else | collective; required by create_product.

config_fields.name: when_made
config_fields.help: createDraftListing when_made for new listings, e.g. made_to_order, 2020_2026, 2010_2019, before_2007; required by create_product.

config_fields.name: shipping_profile_id
config_fields.help: Shipping profile id for new physical listings (GET /v3/application/shops/{shop_id}/shipping-profiles); required for physical listings.

config_fields.name: readiness_state_id
config_fields.help: Processing profile id for new physical listings (GET /v3/application/shops/{shop_id}/readiness-state-definitions); required for physical listings.

config_fields.name: return_policy_id
config_fields.help: Optional return policy id for new listings (GET /v3/application/shops/{shop_id}/policies/return).

adapter.terms: Etsy Open API v3 (per-app rate limits apply; 429 when exceeded); money values are {amount, divisor, currency_code} in minor units.

me.note: GET /v3/application/users/me (scope shops_r) returns {user_id, shop_id} for the seller who granted the token.

list_products.note: GET /v3/application/shops/{shop_id}/listings?state (active|inactive|sold_out|draft|expired; Etsy defaults to active)&limit(1-100)&offset (scope listings_r). `price` is price.amount in MINOR units - divide by price.divisor (usually 100): 1999 = 19.99 in price.currency_code. created_at / updated_at are epoch seconds.

get_product.note: GET /v3/application/listings/{listing_id}; `price` is in minor units (see list_products).

create_product.note: Creates a DRAFT listing (not published) with createDraftListing (form-encoded, scope listings_w): title = name, description (REQUIRED by Etsy - always pass it), price in the shop's currency as a decimal (e.g. 19.99; `currency` is ignored because the shop currency applies), quantity fixed at 1, type physical, and who_made / when_made / taxonomy_id / shipping_profile_id / readiness_state_id / return_policy_id from config. `url` is ignored. Publishing needs an image upload (multipart, not mapped) and then state=active.

list_sales.note: GET /v3/application/shops/{shop_id}/transactions?limit&offset (scope transactions_r): one row per sold listing line (transaction_id, receipt_id, listing_id, title, quantity, price {amount, divisor, currency_code} per unit in MINOR units, buyer_user_id, created_timestamp epoch seconds). The endpoint has no date or listing filter, so `since` and `product_id` are not sent; buyer emails are not exposed.

not_offered.update_price: Listing prices live in the inventory offerings: updateListingInventory (PUT /v3/application/listings/{listing_id}/inventory) must resend the entire products array with every offering's price, quantity and is_enabled (https://developers.etsy.com/documentation/reference#operation/updateListingInventory), which one call from a product id and price cannot build.
not_offered.get_sales_stats: Open API v3 has no revenue summary; the payment ledger (getShopPaymentAccountLedgerEntries) lists individual entries between required min_created / max_created epoch bounds (https://developers.etsy.com/documentation/reference#operation/getShopPaymentAccountLedgerEntries).
not_offered.list_refunds: There is no refunds collection; refunds appear inside each ShopReceipt's refunds[] (https://developers.etsy.com/documentation/reference#operation/getShopReceipts).
not_offered.refund: The Open API v3 reference has no refund operation; refunds are issued in Shop Manager (https://developers.etsy.com/documentation/reference).

evidence: host api.etsy.com: DNS ok, TLSv1.2 (GlobalSign nv-sa)
probe: 5/5 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 404 (not_found), so the answers are path-specific
token api.etsy.com/v3/public/oauth/token: 403 API key not found or not active
spec https://www.etsy.com/openapi/generated/oas/3.0.0.json: 5/5 tools match (path, method, parameters, body keys, response paths)
